author: Anuj Singh Kushwaha
title: Tucker Carlson addresses 2028 presidential run speculation after saying he won't support the Republican Party - NewsBreak
text:
By Anuj Singh Kushwaha ,
9 hours ago
Tucker Carlson, founder of Tucker Carlson Network, speaks on stage on the fourth day of the Republican National Convention at the Fiserv Forum on July 18, 2024 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin © Getty Tucker Carlson, founder of Tucker Carlson Network, speaks on stage on the fourth day of the Republican National Convention at the Fiserv Forum on July 18, 2024 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin - Source: Getty
Tucker Carlson has put an end to speculation about a potential 2028 presidential bid amid his highly publicized rift with the Republican Party.
In recent months, Carlson has turned against President Trump over his administration's foreign policy. The former Fox News star recently appeared on the Can't Be Censored podcast, where he said that he would not support the Republican Party in the upcoming midterms. On Tuesday, Carlson appeared on Alex Jones' show and expanded on the issue after his remarks sparked a debate on social media.
During the interview, Jones also brought up the speculation about Carlson positioning himself as a presidential candidate. Jones showed a Washington Times report claiming that Carlson's odds of becoming president in 2028 had jumped to nearly 10%. Jones then asked the conservative commentator whether he would run in 2028, to which he replied:
"Of course, I'm not planning to run for president. I've never said or done anything that would suggest I have an interest in political office because I don't. I never have had an interest in political office ever. It's just not kind of what I do for a living. It's not what I'm interested in."
Continuing on that note, Alex Jones asked Carlson if he would support JD Vance's candidacy in the next presidential election, adding that he thought Vance was a better choice than Marco Rubio. Carlson agreed with Jones and said:
"Obviously, he's great compared to Rubio. Obviously, look, I'll support the best person. I always have liked JD Vance enormously. I think he's really smart. He's in an impossible situation. I think he's doing his best."
